thought.text: The backend boots all the way to vector store creation, which needs a non-empty Mistral key (constructor validates non-empty, not against the API). Let me check how the config wires the key and whether the vector store service is optional:

reasoning_content:
The backend requires a MistralAI API key at startup in order to build the vector store (used by the chatbot and the HWK pre-check). Without a key it can't even start. This is a documented limitation:

> **AI knowledge base ships empty.** The chatbot and HWK pre-check (KI-Prüfung) require an embedding corpus in the `VectorEmbedding` table. ... Build your own corpus with `tools/pdf-embeddings-generator.js` and configure the source paths in `apps/startuphafen-backend/src/features/common/vector-store.ts`.

The guide says to create a `.localConfigs.json` with `mistral: { apiKey: "" }`. An empty API key will fail. This is a real external dependency (a MistralAI API token, which "can be created in your organization's project on the MistralAI website").

Let me check how the chatbot/HWK routers use the vector store, and whether there's a way to make the server start without a Mistral key. I'll look at VectorStoreService and the router.

The key question is: is this part of "installing the software"? The core application (Angular frontend, Express backend, database, Keycloak auth, ERiC/OZG placeholders) should work. The AI chatbot requires Mistral.

Let me check if there's a config flag to disable the vector store / chatbot, or whether I can provide a dummy Mistral key that allows startup (even if chatbot calls fail at runtime). Actually, the MistralAIEmbeddings constructor throws if the key is empty. If I give a non-empty placeholder key, the constructor will succeed (it doesn't validate the key against the API at construction time), and the server will start. The chatbot would fail at actual query time (401 from Mistral), but the app boots.

Let me check the VectorStoreService and how the config wires up the mistral key.
